question: How does an inline entity reference show it is a link? The product has no inline text-link idiom today — every existing link is a shadcn Button or a nav item — so EntityRef needed one and §5a is unapproved.
best_guess: Underline on hover only, at the existing underline-offset-2, with no colour change and no new token. The global :focus-visible ring in globals.css supplies the keyboard affordance. Nothing new is spent from the palette.

section: FR-80 adoption across the eleven existing screens
question: Once Wave B adopts <EntityRef>, does the existing <Ref>/<RefList> in answer-chips.tsx get deleted, or do both stay? They emit different contracts (data-verify-unit="ref" vs "entity-ref") and the e2e gate only counts the latter, so a screen that keeps Ref reads as un-adopted.
best_guess: Both stay for now; EntityRef supersedes Ref wherever a reference resolves to a real entity, and Ref remains only for identifier tokens that name no entity at all (if any survive). This unit changes no existing screen either way, so the decision costs nothing here and belongs to the adopting units.

question: When a screen renders a unit id like `u4` without naming a run, should resolution refuse, or pick a row?
best_guess: Refuse unless EXACTLY ONE work item in the engagement carries that unit. Zero matches and two-or-more matches both resolve to null and render FR-12's dangling treatment. Supplying `runId` makes it exact. Picking the most recent was rejected: a link that is right most of the time and silently wrong the rest of it is the navigable form of a wrong `done`.

question: What label does an entity reference carry when the row exists and has no human reference of its own — a `hand`-mode work item with no unit, a blocker with a null `ref`?
best_guess: `<kind> <first 8 chars of uuid>` — e.g. `work item 3f2a1b8c` — from one exported `fallbackLabel()`. The uuid is the only identity the row has and §7a leaves `id` clear on all three affected tables. Rendering an empty token or dropping the reference were both rejected as silent.

question: FR-80 names `an engagement slug` among the references that must be navigable, but `engagement` is not one of FR-81's eight kinds, so `ENTITY_KINDS` has no entry for it and `<EntityRef>` cannot render one. Which requirement gives?
best_guess: Leave the seam alone and report it. `tests/m27-gate.test.ts` asserts `ENTITY_KINDS` equals exactly FR-81's eight, so adding `engagement` turns a passing gate red. The engagement detail view already exists at `/registry/[slug]` and is already linked from the registry table, so Wave C renders a plain `<Link href={`/registry/${slug}`}>` — every detail loader returns `engagement.slug` for exactly that. FR-80 is met in substance; the reference is simply not an `<EntityRef>`.

question: Should a requirement's detail view also list the contract milestones whose acceptance criteria name it — a fifth relationship beyond FR-82's four?
best_guess: Load it and let Wave C decide whether to render it. It is an FR-81 inbound reference and it is already stored (`acceptance_criterion.requirement_ref`); nothing new is derived. Only `id` and `name` are read — no amount is decrypted — and the path is operator-only, so FR-86 is unaffected. Returned as `RequirementDetail.milestones`, named distinctly from FR-82's four so it cannot be mistaken for one of them.

question: Should the contract-milestone detail view show FR-50/FR-51's `billable` / `claimed` / `open` state?
best_guess: No, and deliberately. FR-81 asks for fields and references; the invoice gate is derived by `committedAnswer` and a second implementation of it on a detail view is exactly the drift FR-82's `nothing new is derived` clause exists to prevent. If the view wants it, it comes from `readCommitted` and not from a copy. Stated rather than silently omitted.

question: Two migrations disagree about whether `open_question` has a natural key. Which does the resolver honour?
best_guess: Both are recorded and the later one is implemented. `20260819144331`'s table comment says `No natural unique key, deliberately`; `20260819165903` then added `source_key` (`<artifact filename>#<ordinal>`, clear text) and `20260819170622` made its unique index plain. So resolution by `(engagement_id, source_key)` is supported. It is a MACHINE key — no screen renders a filename and an ordinal — and the support is expected to go unused: zero migrations hold a foreign key to `open_question` and zero files under `src/app/` mention it, both measured.

question: All eight detail views need a four-state `Prose` renderer and a plain engagement link, but no Wave C unit owns `src/components/` — should these be factored into one `src/components/detail-prose.tsx` once Wave C has merged?
best_guess: Duplicated the two primitives inside the three route trees f1 owns rather than creating a new shared file three parallel units would each create and collide on. Recommend a follow-up unit factoring them out after the merge.

question: What words should `unreadable` and `not-requested` use, so that eight views written by three units do not show the same failure three different ways?
best_guess: `unreadable` (the word `registry-display.ts`'s UNREADABLE_AMOUNT already uses, drawn in the same `text-state-blocked font-semibold` treatment milestone-table.tsx gives an amount that did not decrypt) and `not read` for `not-requested`, drawn quietly because nothing is wrong. f2 and f3 should be pointed at these rather than choosing their own.

question: Where should a detail view's back link point when the entity has no listing screen of its own? There is no `/defects` and no `/blockers` index, only the `[id]` segments.
best_guess: Back to the answer screen the entity appears on: work item to /work-items, defect to /broken, blocker to /blocked. No index route was invented, because FR-81 asks for detail views and inventing two listing screens is scope this unit does not hold.

question: i1's finding 1 and ruling 3 both leave the engagement as a plain link rather than a ninth entity kind. Confirming that FR-80's `engagement slug` is met in substance by /registry/<slug> and needs no further work in M2.7.
best_guess: Rendered as a plain next/link carrying data-verify-unit="detail-engagement" and data-verify-slug, never an <EntityRef>. Adding a ninth kind would turn gate test 1 red.

section: CR-003 FR-81 / ruling 4 — milestones on the requirement view
question: What should the milestone section on /requirements/[id] be called so it cannot be mistaken for a fifth FR-82 relationship?
best_guess: Heading 'Contract acceptance', data-verify-unit='requirement-acceptance' (not 'requirement-milestones'), with a note on the section saying it is FR-81's inbound side and not one of FR-82's four. Names only, never amounts.

section: §7a Prose — four states, five Wave C views
question: Where should the four-state Prose renderer live, given that five of Wave C's eight detail views render a Prose field and no unit owns src/components/?
best_guess: Keep it inside my own tree at src/app/requirements/_components/detail-prose.tsx and import it from the questions view; flag for consolidation into src/components/detail-prose.tsx after Wave C merges. Creating a file in src/components/ would collide with three other units doing the same thing in parallel.

section: §5a state scale — FR-47 self-certification on the tests section
question: FR-47 self-certification has no token of its own; engagement-coverage.tsx already draws its self-certified count in state-unproven (tone='warn'). Should the requirement view's per-test self-certified marker follow that, giving state-unproven two meanings?
best_guess: Follow the existing precedent exactly rather than introduce a token — the overload predates this unit and inventing a colour is the thing the brief forbids outright. Reported as an inherited overload rather than a new decision.

question: DetailSection only forwards verifyUnit, so a count cannot be published on the same element the e2e gate queries. Where should the four relationship counts go?
best_guess: One uniform child contract per section: data-verify-unit='relation-count' with data-verify-relation and data-verify-count, so all four counts answer one query and the gate's four section names stay exactly as asserted. No edit to entity-detail.tsx.

question: i1 measured that nothing in the product points at an open question (zero foreign keys, zero files under src/app/). Should /questions/[id] ship as a route reachable only by typing a uuid?
best_guess: Build it — FR-81 names open_question as one of the eight and gate test 2 enumerates all eight — and report the unreachability plainly rather than adding an unrequested listing screen to fix it.

question: On external_wait, release and contract_milestone the entity's human reference IS its title (the wait label, the release identifier, the milestone name), so <EntityDetail title> and <EntityDetail identifier> render the same string twice. Should identifier be omitted when it equals the title?
best_guess: Pass it anyway. `identifier` has no omit state — undefined renders `Absent` with 'this row carries no reference of its own', which would be a false claim about a row whose label IS its reference. The duplication is cosmetic; the false absence is not.

question: This repo has TWO money formatters that disagree on shape: `formatAmount` in registry-display.ts renders `$111.00` (Intl, locale pinned to en-US) and `money` in money-display.ts renders `111.00 USD` (fixed format, ISO code after the figure). /registry/[slug] uses the first and /committed the second, so the same milestone amount reads two ways on two screens. Which one is the product's answer?
best_guess: Used `formatAmount`, because the f3 brief names it explicitly and because /milestones/[id] is entered from /registry/[slug]. Flagged rather than resolved: money-display.ts is in this run's no-edit list, and unifying them is a decision about a screen f3 does not own.

question: `deployedAt` is a timestamp and this view renders it at day resolution via `formatDate`. Deployments happen several times a day, so a day is sometimes not enough to order two releases. Should it render at minute resolution instead?
best_guess: Day resolution. The brief says to use `formatDate` and not to format dates by hand, and `isoMinute` — the only minute-resolution helper — carries the zone-less-timestamp bug measured in this unit's report. Ordering releases within a day is not a requirement M2.7 states.

question: Adopting <EntityRef> moves three prose-styled tokens into the entity-ref mono chip: an external wait's label on /blocked, and a milestone's name on /committed, /next and /bottleneck. Is the chip right for a free-text label and a milestone name, or should those keep their current type treatment and carry the contract another way?
best_guess: Use the chip everywhere. It is Wave A's decision about what an entity reference looks like in this product, and three spellings of a reference on six screens is the drift the shared component exists to prevent. Recorded as the one visual change on these screens.

question: BlockedItem.blockerRef is in the payload and is NOT rendered on /blocked today. FR-80 names 'a blocker ref' among the references that must be navigable. Should /blocked start rendering it beside the existing 'Held by:' line so a blocker becomes navigable?
best_guess: No. FR-80 governs every reference 'rendered on any screen', and this one is not rendered; adding it is a new design decision under a §5a that is explicitly NOT APPROVED. /blocked still emits work_item and external_wait references, so the gate's count is satisfied without it. Left for Erik.

question: `blockedAnswer` builds each wait's `blocks` entry as `item.unit ?? item.id`, so the list mixes unit keys with raw uuids and nothing distinguishes them. Asked as work-unit references, the uuid entries resolve to nothing and render dangling even though the row exists. Should the payload carry the id and the label separately (an edit to src/lib/server/answers/blocked.ts, which this unit may not make)?
best_guess: Leave it dangling and report it. Sniffing the string for a uuid shape would be inferring which of two meanings a value carries, which is the guess this product refuses; and a `hand`/`external` work item blocked by a wait is exactly the row that would be linked wrongly. Recorded as a finding.

question: No answer payload carries an `engagementId`; every one carries the slug only. Resolving any text reference therefore costs one extra `engagement` read per screen render (`listEngagements()`), purely to translate slug to uuid. Should `src/lib/server/answers/*` carry `engagementId` on its answer types instead?
best_guess: Pay the extra read for now. `src/lib/server/answers/**` is outside this unit's ownership, `listEngagements()` is an existing operator-gated read that /registry already makes, and the alternative touches six answer types five parallel units render against. Named in the report as a new read per B29.

question: `contestingDefects` and `unclassifiedDefects` are defect uuids and are rendered only as counts on the contested and unclassified chips. Should those counts expand into navigable defect references?
best_guess: No. A count is what the screen renders today and expanding it is a layout decision, not an adoption. The defects are all reachable from /broken, which does render them as navigable D-nn.

question: `Ref` and `RefList` in src/components/answer-chips.tsx now have no caller anywhere in src/ or tests/ outside that file. Should they be deleted, and if so by whom?
best_guess: Leave them. Ruling 7 says a conclusion that they should be deleted is a finding and not an edit, and f5's screens may still hold the last callers in a worktree this unit cannot see. Reported rather than removed.

question: Two of the eight /work-items filters (Evidence, Unautomated) emit STORED enum spellings into the URL that parseWorkItemQuery then rejects, so selecting one shows an unfiltered list under a 'not recognised' banner and FR-84 cannot restore it. Fix it in my files with the existing toWire(), or leave it red as an out-of-scope defect for a later unit?
best_guess: Fix it. Both files are mine (_lib/query.ts, _components/filter-bar.tsx), toWire() exists for exactly this, and FR-84 is provably broken for those two filters without it. I did NOT widen UNAUTOMATED_REASON or EVIDENCE_SCOPE in rules.ts — that file is not mine and widening a closed set is the failure CLAUDE.md names.

question: listWorkItems carries blocker_id and external_wait_id as uuids but no blocker.ref and no external_wait.label, so those two references render as fallbackLabel ('blocker cccccccc'). Should detail-load.ts export a batch label reader (i1 has labelEntities and refFromId internally, unexported) so listings can name them properly?
best_guess: Render fallbackLabel. It is ruling 2's only sanctioned fallback, the reference is navigable either way, and widening either src/lib/detail-load.ts or src/lib/server/workitems/list.ts is another unit's file.

section: FR-80 / spec 5a typography — milestone names and wait labels
question: contract_milestone.name and external_wait.label are natural keys, so FR-80 makes them references — but they are prose-ish ('Phase 1 delivery'), and <EntityRef> renders the `ident` monospace token. Is monospace right for these two, or should they stay sans and carry the link some other way?
best_guess: Adopt <EntityRef> and pass className='text-sm font-medium' so size and weight are unchanged; the face becomes mono. They ARE the columns resolveRefs looks these rows up by, so spec 5a's 'identifiers are monospace' covers them. Named as the one visual change beyond navigability.

section: FR-12 / FR-83 — two known/unknown answers on one acceptance reference
question: AcceptanceRefs now carries M1.3's data-verify-known (FR-12: is it ingested?) and a nested entity-ref data-verify-known (FR-83: did it resolve to exactly one row?). Is keeping both correct, or should one be dropped?
best_guess: Keep both and add data-verify-unresolved as the count. They answer different questions, the brief said to add the entity-ref contract alongside rather than replace it, and where two artifacts disagree this product records both.
